purpose: The remaining build work, in the order it can be done, each item sourced to the measurement that justifies it. Tuning is deliberately last - see deferred_tuning.

items.title: Fix the eager-path doorbell payload so the in-engine profiler works
items.status: done 2026-10-21: the profiler works on this CUDA build (31 of 31 requests printed a stage table, 0 payload errors); the failure was A770/SYCL-only (docs/WINDOW_PROFILE_CUDA.md)
items.detail: STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE and STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER both fail with 'verify: layer 0 rang but its payload never arrived whole', reproducibly 3/3. Likely defect: the eager path does not publish the doorbell payload doorbell_payload_ready waits for, so the host spins to the 2 s timeout. Debug-only path; normal graph-mode inference is unaffected.
items.caveat: recorded on the A770/SYCL build. Confirm it reproduces on this CUDA build before treating it as the same bug.
items.done_when: either the profiler produces per-stage timings on this CUDA build, or the failure is confirmed A770-only and item 3 proceeds on item 2's numbers alone

items.title: Measure the doorbell round-trip latency (ring -> host -> flag -> GPU) and how much of the window is idle GPU time
items.status: done 2026-10-21: doorbell round trip (waitA) 0.32 ms/window, 0.5% of a 59.4 ms window; the GPU waits 65.4% of the window, 59.2% of it on the PCIe-share copies (waitB) and 6.0% on the CPU pool (docs/WINDOW_PROFILE_CUDA.md, tools/read_window_profile.py)
items.source: docs/A770_SPEED_SPEC.md, end of 'GPU utilization: the GPU is mostly IDLE during decode'
items.done_when: a measured round-trip latency in ms and a measured idle-GPU fraction on this machine, from interleaved runs with state capture, against the 24.3% floor

items.title: Overlap the CPU expert pool with GPU work during decode
items.status: needs a decision before it starts: items 1 and 2 put the CPU-pool wait at 6.0% of the window, so hiding it completely cannot clear the 24.3% gate; the time is in waitB, the PCIe-share copies (docs/WINDOW_PROFILE_CUDA.md). Retarget to the bus share and copy path, or close
items.source: docs/A770_SPEED_SPEC.md, 'The window is nearly GPU + CPU serial (architectural hypothesis)' and 'Per-stage breakdown obtained (decisive)'
items.detail: on the A770 the wait-for-CPU-flag stages plus copy-and-combine are ~87% of the window and every actual GPU kernel is small; worker count was already tried and did nothing, so it is a scheduling change, not a sizing one.
items.caveat: the 87% figure is from the Arc card over PCIe 3.0 x4, not from this machine. The shape is the same - decode here is CPU-bound, and this card idles at 20-72% during runs - but the size is not transferred.
items.done_when: the window shrinks by more than the 24.3% floor under the interleaved control, with the idle-GPU fraction from item 2 visibly falling as the cause

items.title: Run cache-off on the non-agent suite
items.status: open, the only place the -34% has never been measured
items.done_when: six launches, interleaved, engine logs checked arm by arm - and the -34% either reproduces on this suite or the two suites are stated as disagreeing

items.title: Write up the adapt-kv sweep honestly: nothing separated
items.status: done 2026-10-21 (b63be2eb): both write-ups carry the same verdict, nothing separated; every number reproduces through tools/read_sweep_warm.py
items.detail: 13 arms, three runs each, all within their own noise. The biggest arm gap (72.6%, adapt-swaps 16) sits inside the noise row's own per-turn range (54-98%), so the data cannot separate them and the honest verdict is 'nothing separated', not a story about which arm won. Cache-off is the contrast: its arm (28-44%) lies wholly outside its repeats (1-24%).
items.done_when: docs/SWEEP_ADAPT_KV.md and bench/results/ab-adapt-kv-sweep/SWEEP_ADAPT_KV.md tell the same story, and every number in both reproduces through tools/summarize_ab_sweep.py or tools/read_sweep_warm.py

deferred_tuning.why: the sweep that tried to settle these produced nothing above its own floor, so tuning now would be fitting noise and the decision would have to be re-made after the build anyway
already_settled_do_not_resweep: no gain: --kv k8v4, --prefill auto:16384, a smaller VRAM reserve, --adapt-async

open_knobs.note: real lever, already automatic - leave it unset unless the experiment is about the bus share
real lever, already measured as a wash on the A770; do not re-open as a sizing question
real lever, its own experiment with its own parity gate, never a side effect of a memory sweep

deferred_tuning.gate: any arm must clear the 24.3% floor under the interleaved control, and the tool must compute that verdict rather than assert it

execution.mode: end-to-end by Claude, no per-package review
execution.my_role: recommendations are binding as recommendations - take them, but a gate that fails stops the item and gets reported, not worked around
rules: one change per commit, message says what was measured, not what was hoped
every number written into a doc must reproduce off disk with the tool of record named in the doc
the verdict line in any tool must be computed, never asserted
numbers already in the docs are correct as written - do not re-derive them from rounded medians
run tools/test_strata_ab.py before committing; it must stay at 31 passing
order_of_work: item 5 first - it needs no GPU and it is the write-up the others get judged against
then item 2, the latency measurement, which needs no profiler and unblocks item 3
item 1 in parallel, since it gates the profiler that item 3 wants
item 4 whenever the machine is free
item 3 last, and only after 1 and 2 have produced numbers

handoff.note: the two are different documents and should stay separate - one says what to build, the other says what to run to check a piece that got built
